## Source of truth

The repository remains the source of truth. The knowledge index is derived state.

## Provenance

Every assertion should identify whether it is:

- observed: derived directly from repository/tool output
- declared: explicitly supplied by a human/project artifact
- inferred: model/system interpretation
- generated: derived artifact such as summaries or maps

Do not silently upgrade inferred information to canonical truth.

## Identity

Logical IDs should be stable across source-file moves. Example:


```text

to

provenance
metadata
```

- HAS_VALUE_OBJECT

- IMPORTS

- REQUIRES

- CONSUMES

A 900-line source file can describe one knowledge node but expose only a 20-line method as the relevant evidence. Nodes describe structure; fragments control context cost.

# Contributing

## Ground rules

- Keep changes focused; don't refactor unrelated code in a feature change.
- Tests first where practical; every bug gets a regression test.
- Core crates stay agent-agnostic and language-agnostic.
- Git and the filesystem are the source of truth; the SQLite index is derived and rebuildable.

## Prerequisites

- Rust stable with `rustfmt` and `clippy`
- Git on `PATH` (tests create temporary repositories)

## Definition of green

```bash
scripts/check.sh
```

which runs:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

## Code style

- Libraries use typed errors (`thiserror`); only the CLI binary uses `anyhow`.
- Log with `tracing`. Only `crates/agentos-cli/src/output.rs` writes to stdout/stderr.
- Sort collections before emitting; no timestamps in golden outputs.
- Document every public item (`missing_docs` is enforced through clippy `-D warnings`).
- Prefer deep modules: define the trait and its contract tests before the implementation.

## Tests and fixtures

- Unit tests live next to the code; CLI end-to-end tests in `crates/agentos-cli/tests/`.
- `agentos-testkit` (dev-dependency only) provides `TempProject`, `CliRunner` and the fixture
  loader (`fixture_path`, `copy_fixture`).
- Fixtures live in `fixtures/<name>/` with ground truth in `expected/` (see `fixtures/README.md`).
- Evaluation cases live in `evals/<area>/` (see `evals/README.md`); run them with
  `agentos evaluate <area>`.
- Built-in skills live in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and are compiled into the binary. Each needs the
  body sections `When to use`, `Inputs`, `Procedure` (numbered), `Outputs`, `Must not`, `Validation`
  and at least one `eval_cases` entry; `agentos skills validate` fails otherwise. When a router case
  fails, tune the skill's `triggers`, never the expected answer.

## Database migrations

Migrations for the core `meta` table are listed in `crates/agentos-core/src/db.rs` (`MIGRATIONS`).
Append new core migrations with the next version number; never edit or reorder a released migration.
The knowledge graph uses its own migration table inside the same `agentos.db` (`agentos-knowledge`),
because `agentos-core` cannot depend on that crate.

# AgentOS

AgentOS is a local-first, agent-agnostic engineering intelligence layer. It gives coding agents
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any other) the right knowledge, skills, workflow, feedback and
guardrails for a task — without replacing the agent.

> Status: **early development**. The CLI can initialise a project, manage portable skills, build a
> derived knowledge graph, assemble a budgeted Context Pack, and run validation providers. Workflow
> and the other engines are not implemented yet.

## Build

Requirements: Rust (stable, edition 2024) and Git. SQLite is bundled; no system install needed.

```bash
cargo build --release
./target/release/agentos --version
```

## Usage

```bash
agentos init              # create .agentos/ (config, profile, derived SQLite index); safe to re-run
agentos doctor            # check root, git, .agentos, config, database, writability
agentos doctor --json     # same, machine-readable
agentos config            # effective configuration and the source of every value

agentos project profile          # classification, maturity, signals (written by init and scan)
agentos scan                     # index the repository; a second run reports 0 changed
agentos knowledge stats          # node, edge and provenance counts
agentos knowledge nodes          # logical ids
agentos knowledge edges
agentos knowledge inspect <id>
agentos knowledge rebuild        # delete the derived graph and scan again

agentos skills list               # skills that won discovery, with level and invocation
agentos skills inspect tdd        # metadata, resolved dependencies, permissions, body
agentos skills inspect tdd --brief  # metadata only; the body is not read
agentos skills validate           # everything, including bodies; exit 3 on errors
agentos skills install ./my-skill # copy a local skill into .agents/skills/ (git URLs: not yet)
agentos skills graph [--format dot]
agentos domain scan               # infer domain nodes; never confirms them
agentos domain contexts
agentos domain terminology
agentos domain map
agentos domain propose            # one lifecycle step toward Proposed
agentos domain confirm <id>       # Proposed → Confirmed, or Confirmed → Canonical
agentos domain reject <id>
agentos domain validate           # exit 3 when canonical evidence has drifted
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
                              # naive file-token baseline; writes evals/baselines/context-baseline.json
agentos context explain "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos context build "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --format json
agentos context stats "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos evaluate skills           # run evals/skills; exit 3 if a case fails
agentos evaluate knowledge        # project profiles and language graph fixtures
agentos evaluate ddd              # domain lifecycle fixtures
agentos evaluate context          # context packs against evals/context
agentos validate detect           # providers selected for this project
agentos validate --kind unit_test --json
agentos validate last             # most recently stored result
agentos validate record-regression <id>
                              # write evals/feedback/<id>.json from a failed result
agentos architecture analyze     # detectors over the knowledge graph; exit 3 if any finding
agentos evaluate feedback         # detection, parsing, permission, regressions
agentos evaluate architecture     # bad and good architecture fixtures
agentos plan "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --workflow feature
agentos run <plan-id> --runner mock
agentos run status <run-id>
agentos run resume <run-id>
agentos run abort <run-id>
agentos evaluate workflow         # plans, scheduler, resume, fix loop
```

Global flags: `--root <PATH>`, `--json`, `-v` / `-vv`, `--log-level <FILTER>`.

### Skills

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md`: YAML front-matter (schema:
[`schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json`](schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json)) plus a markdown body.
Discovery locations, highest priority first:

1. `<root>/.agents/skills/`
2. `<root>/.agentos/skills/`
3. user-level: `--user-skills-dir`, else `AGENTOS_USER_SKILLS_DIR`, else `$HOME/.agentos/skills`
4. built-in skills compiled into `agentos` (from `skills/`; replace with `--builtin-skills-dir` /
   `AGENTOS_BUILTIN_SKILLS_DIR`)

A higher level overrides a lower one. Two skills with the same name at the same level are an error,
and a broken skill hides lower-level copies of the same name instead of silently falling back.

Invocation: `user_invocable` (default `true`) and `model_invocable` (default `false`) are separate.
A model-invocable skill may not require, or route to, a skill that is only user-invocable.
Permissions (`fs.read`, `fs.write`, `shell`, `network`, `browser`) are default-deny.

### Project root

`--root` if given, otherwise the Git top-level of the current directory, otherwise the current
directory.

### Configuration

Resolved per key, later layers winning:

1. built-in defaults
2. `.agentos/config.toml`
3. environment: `AGENTOS_LOG` (`log.level`), `AGENTOS_OUTPUT` (`output.format`)
4. CLI flags: `--log-level` / `-v` / `-vv`, `--json`

| Key | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | `warn` | a level (`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`) or tracing directives such as `agentos_core=debug,warn` |
| `output.format` | `text` | `text`, `json` |

Logs are written to stderr; command results to stdout.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | runtime error |
| 2 | usage error |
| 3 | a check failed: `doctor` critical failure, `skills validate` errors, `evaluate` case failures, a workflow run that is `failed` or `blocked` |

### Project state

```text
.agentos/
├── config.toml          # project configuration (yours to edit; never overwritten)
├── .gitignore           # keeps derived state out of Git
├── project-profile.json # derived classification and signals; rewritten by init and scan
├── agentos.db           # SQLite knowledge index: derived state, safe to delete and rebuild
├── context-cache/       # derived Context Pack cache
├── feedback/            # derived validation results
└── runs/                # derived plans and resumable runs
```

## Development

```bash
scripts/check.sh   # cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

# Architecture

The locked V1 architecture is specified in [spec/ARCHITECTURE.md](spec/ARCHITECTURE.md), with
product principles in [spec/VISION.md](spec/VISION.md) and per-subsystem contracts in `spec/`.

## What exists after Phase 6

Phase 6 adds `agentos-workflow`. It plans a task graph, expands skill dependencies through the
Phase 1 resolver, builds one Phase 4 Context Pack per step, and consumes Phase 5
`ValidationResult` values. Runs are files under `.agentos/runs/`. `MockRunner` is the test
executor. `ManualRunner` prints the step and records a supplied result. There is no model call
and no agent adapter.

## What exists after Phase 5

Phase 5 adds `agentos-feedback` and `agentos-tools`. Validation providers construct commands and
parse output. Every process is started by `agentos-tools` after a shell permission check, with a
timeout and a byte cap on stdout and stderr. Architecture analysis reads the existing knowledge
graph. It does not create another one. Stored results live under `.agentos/feedback/` and are
derived state.

## What exists after Phase 4

Phase 4 adds `agentos-context`. It reads the Phase 2 and Phase 3 graph and returns a Context Pack.
It does not write a second graph. `agentos benchmark baseline` measures naive file tokens before
any pack is built. `agentos context build` projects logical ids, provenance, and lifecycle status
into a pack with a retrieval trace. A cache under `.agentos/context-cache/` is derived state.

## What exists after Phase 3

Phase 3 adds a domain module in `agentos-knowledge`. It writes bounded contexts, tactical concepts,
findings, and lifecycle transitions into the same SQLite index (`domain_nodes`, `domain_edges`,
`domain_transitions`, `domain_findings`). Software nodes stay in the Phase 2 tables. `agentos domain`
confirms or rejects them. Generated markdown is under `.agentos/knowledge/domain/`.

## Crate layout

```text
agentos-cli ─┬─► agentos-config ───► agentos-core
             ├─► agentos-knowledge ─► agentos-core
             ├─► agentos-context ──► agentos-knowledge
             ├─► agentos-skills ─┬─► agentos-core
             │                   └─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-feedback ─┬─► agentos-knowledge
             │                     ├─► agentos-permissions
             │                     └─► agentos-tools ─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-workflow ─┬─► agentos-skills
             │                     ├─► agentos-context
             │                     ├─► agentos-feedback
             │                     ├─► agentos-permissions
             │                     └─► agentos-tools
             └─► agentos-evaluation ─┬─► agentos-core
                                     ├─► agentos-knowledge
                                     ├─► agentos-context
                                     ├─► agentos-skills
                                     ├─► agentos-permissions
                                     ├─► agentos-feedback
                                     ├─► agentos-tools
                                     └─► agentos-workflow
```

| Crate | Contents |
|---|---|
| `agentos-core` | `fs` (`FileSystem` incl. sorted `read_dir` and streaming `open_read`, `RealFs`, `MemFs`), `git` (`Git`, `GitCli`, `FakeGit`), `root` (project-root detection), `state` (`.agentos/` layout, idempotent `ensure`), `db` (SQLite open, migration runner, read-only `inspect`) |
| `agentos-config` | Layered config resolution (defaults → file → env → CLI) with per-key sources |
| `agentos-permissions` | `Capability`, `PermissionSet`, `PermissionSubject`, `check(subject, capability) -> Decision` (default-deny, with reason) |
| `agentos-skills` | `SKILL.md` front-matter parsing (schema `schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json` + semantic checks), `SkillLoader` (prioritized discovery, front-matter only), `SkillRegistry` (lazy body/reference loading), dependency resolver (topological order, cycle path, semver), rule-based `SkillRouter`, full `validate`, `SkillGraph` (text/DOT), local `install`, built-in skills embedded from `skills/` |
| `agentos-knowledge` | Automatic project profile, ignore-aware scanner, `LanguageExtractor` (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, Ruby), knowledge graph in SQLite (nodes, edges, fragments, FTS5), provenance, domain tables |
| `agentos-context` | Context Pack assembly over that graph: intent, routing, lexical/graph retrieval, budget, trace, cache. `NullSemantic` is the semantic seam |
| `agentos-evaluation` | Deterministic case runner; areas `skills`, `knowledge`, `ddd`, `context`, `feedback`, `architecture`, and `workflow` |
| `agentos-feedback` | `ValidationProvider`, language providers, stored results, architecture detectors over the existing graph |
| `agentos-tools` | Process runner: shell permission, timeout, capped stdout and stderr |
| `agentos-workflow` | Task graph, Phase 1 skill expansion, deterministic scheduler, resumable runs, MockRunner and ManualRunner |
| `agentos-cli` | The `agentos` binary: `init`, `doctor`, `config`, `project profile`, `scan`, `knowledge`, `domain`, `benchmark baseline`, `context`, `skills`, `validate`, `architecture analyze`, `plan`, `run`, `evaluate {skills, knowledge, ddd, context, feedback, architecture, workflow}` |
| `agentos-testkit` | Dev-only: `TempProject`, `CliRunner`, fixture loader |
| all other crates | Compiling stubs, implemented by later phases |

### Skill system data flow

```text
SkillLocation × 4 ─► SkillLoader::discover ─► Discovery { registry, diagnostics }
  (front-matter only)                              │
                 ┌─────────────┬──────────────┬────┴────────┬──────────────┐
           resolve(name)   SkillRouter     check(cap)    validate()     SkillGraph
           topo order      ranked+reasons  allow/deny    + bodies       text / dot
```

Bodies are read only by `Skill::load_body` (used by `inspect` without `--brief` and by `validate`);
reference files only by `Skill::load_reference`. Nothing in the skill system executes a skill or
calls a model.
# AgentOS Architecture (locked for V1)

## Product boundary

AgentOS is a local-first, agent-agnostic engineering intelligence and workflow layer. It augments coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. It is not itself the primary coding-agent UI.

## Project layout

```text
agentos/
├── README.md  CONTRIBUTING.md  Cargo.toml
├── crates/
│   ├── agentos-cli  agentos-core  agentos-config  agentos-knowledge
│   ├── agentos-context  agentos-skills  agentos-workflow  agentos-memory
│   ├── agentos-feedback  agentos-evaluation  agentos-permissions  agentos-tools
│   └── agentos-adapters/{generic,cursor,claude,codex}
├── skills/
├── schemas/
├── fixtures/
├── evals/
├── docs/
└── scripts/
```

## Technology adapters
Language/test-runner/build knowledge lives behind capability interfaces: *what language is this? how do I parse it? run tests? type-check? lint?* The core depends on these interfaces, never on concrete commands.

## Project state layout
```text
.agentos/
├── config.toml
├── agentos.db            # SQLite, derived index (rebuildable)
├── project-profile.json  # Phase 2 (derived)
├── skills/               # project-managed skills (optional)
├── knowledge/domain/     # generated markdown (Phase 3)
├── memory/               # Phase 7
└── runs/                 # Phase 6+ run state and artifacts
```
Portable skills live in `.agents/skills/`.

## Technology
| Component | Choice |
|---|---|
| Core + CLI | Rust (Cargo workspace), single native binary |
| Knowledge store | SQLite |
| Search | SQLite FTS5 + structural/graph; optional embeddings later behind a trait |
| Code parsing | Tree-sitter (introduced Phase 2) |
| Config | TOML for project config; YAML front-matter where a portable skill format requires it |
| Skills | Portable `SKILL.md` packages; project-local `.agents/skills/` |
| Project state | `.agentos/` |
| Git | Git CLI behind an abstraction; libgit2 optional |
| Testing | Rust tests + fixture projects + golden tests |
| Evaluation | Custom deterministic evaluation harness |
| Browser | Capability abstraction; Playwright adapter in Phase 8 |
| Agent integration | Adapter architecture in Phase 9 |

## Core principles

1. Source artifacts remain the source of truth.
2. The knowledge graph is derived/indexed state.
3. Core interfaces are technology-agnostic and agent-agnostic.
4. Context is retrieved progressively and budgeted explicitly.
5. Skills are portable `SKILL.md` packages.
6. Permissions are explicit and default-deny.
7. Inferred domain knowledge never silently becomes canonical.
8. Every important assertion and relationship has provenance.
9. Deterministic behavior is preferred for discovery, routing, retrieval, and evaluation.
10. New infrastructure requires measured justification.

## High-level architecture

```text
CLI / Agent entrypoint
        |
        v
+-----------------------+
| AgentOS Core          |
+-----------+-----------+
            |
   +--------+---------+----------------+
   |        |         |                |
   v        v         v                v
Project   Knowledge Context   Skills   Workflow
Understand  Engine    Engine   Engine  Engine
   |        |         |                |
   +--------+---------+----------------+
            |
            v
      Feedback Engine
            |
            v
   Tools / Capabilities
            |
            v
   Agent-specific adapters
```

## Storage boundary

```text
Git/filesystem = source of truth
SQLite          = derived index/state/evaluation records
```

Human-readable artifacts such as ADRs, ubiquitous-language docs, context maps, and phase reports remain plain files.

## Project understanding

Project understanding runs before or alongside knowledge extraction and is automatic; the user does not choose “greenfield” vs “existing” as a setup step. It produces a deterministic, evidence-backed project profile that downstream phases consume.

The profile has two dimensions:

- `classification`: `GREENFIELD`, `EXISTING`, or `HYBRID`
- `maturity`: `EMPTY`, `SPECIFIED`, `SKELETON`, `DEVELOPING`, `ESTABLISHED`, or `MATURE`

The detector records the signals used (Git history, source files, build/package manifests, tests, docs/specs, schema/API definitions, CI/container config) plus confidence. Classification is descriptive; the maturity/profile must never invent business facts. Ambiguous cases remain explicitly uncertain rather than forcing a false classification.

Greenfield, existing, and hybrid projects converge into the same Knowledge Model: existing projects are primarily reverse-engineered from evidence, while greenfield projects can contribute declared/proposed knowledge from requirements and design artifacts.

## Dependency direction

```text
CLI -> subsystem interfaces -> subsystem implementations
Knowledge <- shared domain model
Context -> Knowledge interfaces
Skills -> skill model + capability interfaces
Workflow -> Skills + Context + Feedback
Adapters -> stable AgentOS interfaces
```

Subsystems must not depend on agent-specific adapters. Language-specific behavior lives behind extractor/provider interfaces.

## Deep modules

Each crate should expose the smallest stable interface required by consumers and hide parsing, indexing, ranking, persistence, and execution complexity internally.

# AgentOS Evaluation System

Evaluation is a first-class subsystem beginning in Phase 0.

## Test layers

1. Unit tests
2. Integration tests
3. Fixture repository tests
4. Golden/retrieval tests
5. End-to-end workflow evaluations
6. Adapter compatibility tests
7. Regression tests for every discovered defect

## Fixture philosophy

Fixtures are small, realistic repositories with known ground truth. Include multiple technology stacks and deliberately bad architectures.

Recommended fixtures:
- `python-fastapi/`
- `node-express/`
- `typescript-react/`
- `go/`
- `java/`
- `ruby-rails/`
- `bad-architecture/`

## Golden case shape

```json
{
  "task": "Add retry support to payment webhook processing",
  "must_include": ["domain.payment.entity.Payment"],
  "must_not_include": ["fleet", "analytics"],
  "required_fragments": ["webhook_handler.py", "test_webhook_idempotency.py"]
}
```

Exact thresholds are derived from measured baselines, never invented.

## Core metrics

Knowledge: node precision/recall, edge precision/recall, provenance coverage.
DDD: context detection, terminology ambiguity, invariant mapping, lifecycle correctness.
Context: required-context recall, irrelevant-context rate, token count, reduction versus baseline, latency, reproducibility.
Skills: discovery, routing, dependency correctness, permission enforcement.
Feedback: validation detection and structured diagnostics.
Architecture: known-violation detection.
Workflow: execution order, ready frontier, resume behavior, bounded repair loops.
Memory: retrieval precision, staleness, forget semantics, secret redaction.
Adapters: install, idempotency, compatibility, uninstall safety.

## Evaluation traceability

Every context and major workflow evaluation should make it possible to answer:
- what inputs were used?
- what knowledge was selected?
- what was excluded and why?
- what tools/permissions were granted?
- what validation evidence was produced?

## Release gate

A release is green only when the relevant automated tests and evaluations pass, regression coverage remains green, and all phase gates are approved.

## Additions

**Golden case optional fields:** `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are `null` until the Phase 4 baseline has been measured; only then are they set. Cases also record `fixture`, the deterministic oracle used, and (for context cases) `required_fragments`.

**Eval folders:** `evals/{knowledge,ddd,context,skills,workflow,feedback,architecture,memory,adapters,end-to-end,baselines}/`.

**Evaluate intermediate artifacts, not only final code:** project profile, knowledge graph, context pack, plan, permissions, feedback, final changes.

**Regression rule:** every bug becomes a permanent case (e.g. `evals/context/payment_webhook_007.json` for "Notifications context retrieved for a Payment task"). `agentos evaluate <area>` must keep it green.

**Dashboard (Phase 10):** `agentos evaluate` prints Knowledge / DDD / Context / Skills / Feedback / Adapters sections and an overall PASS/FAIL using REAL measured values; thresholds come from `evals/thresholds.json`, derived from baselines.

**Known-bad fixture:** `fixtures/bad-architecture/` (circular dependencies, fat controllers, DB calls in domain, duplicate terminology, broken invariants, shallow modules, missing tests) with ground truth.
# AgentOS Knowledge Model

## Source of truth

The repository remains the source of truth. The knowledge index is derived state.

## Provenance

Every assertion should identify whether it is:

- observed: derived directly from repository/tool output
- declared: explicitly supplied by a human/project artifact
- inferred: model/system interpretation
- generated: derived artifact such as summaries or maps

Do not silently upgrade inferred information to canonical truth.

## Identity

Logical IDs should be stable across source-file moves. Example:

```text
domain.payment.entity.Payment
```

rather than using only a path-based identifier.

## Edge model

Edges should have:

```text
id
from
relation_type
to
confidence
provenance
metadata
```

Useful relations include:

### Domain

- BELONGS_TO
- CONTAINS
- HAS_ENTITY
- HAS_VALUE_OBJECT
- HAS_AGGREGATE
- CONSTRAINED_BY
- GOVERNS
- CROSS_CONTEXT_TO
- ANTI_CORRUPTS

### Software

- IMPLEMENTS
- EXPOSES
- CALLS
- DEPENDS_ON
- IMPORTS
- ADAPTS
- PROVIDES
- CONSUMES

### Quality

- TESTS
- VERIFIES
- VALIDATES
- VIOLATES

### Engineering

- GOVERNED_BY
- JUSTIFIED_BY
- SUPERSEDES
- CONFLICTS_WITH
- DERIVED_FROM

### Agent

- REQUIRES
- PRODUCES
- CONSUMES
- USES_TOOL
- INVOKES

## Fragment model

Fragments are the units that can be included in a Context Pack.

A fragment should contain:

```text
id
node_id
source_ref
location
content
fingerprint
token_estimate
kind
```

Examples:
- a class body
- a function
- a test case
- an ADR section
- a terminology entry
- an architecture rule

## Why fragments matter

A 900-line source file can describe one knowledge node but expose only a 20-line method as the relevant evidence. Nodes describe structure; fragments control context cost.

## Common node envelope

Every node should conceptually contain:

```text
id
node_type
name
scope
summary
status
provenance
confidence
version
fingerprint
source_refs
retrieval_metadata
payload
```
## Core node types

### Domain

- bounded_context
- entity
- value_object
- aggregate
- invariant
- domain_service
- policy
- domain_event
- terminology

### Software

- source_file
- symbol
- module
- interface
- api
- repository
- database_table
- external_service

### Engineering

- adr
- architecture_component
- constraint
- decision

### Quality

- test
- test_suite
- validation

### Agent

- skill
- tool
- capability

### Memory

- task
- episode
- observation
- lesson
- research
# AgentOS Skill System

## Portable unit

A skill is a directory containing `SKILL.md` and optional references/scripts/assets.

```text
skill-name/
  SKILL.md
  references/
  scripts/
  assets/
```

## Skill quality rule

A skill exists to make an engineering process more predictable, not merely to store prose.

A skill should define:
- when it applies
- what it consumes
- the ordered procedure
- what it produces
- what it must not do
- how it is validated

## Compatibility

Use the Agent Skills / `SKILL.md` shape as the portable contract. Keep agent-specific files in adapters or compatibility directories.
## Invocation modes

### User-invoked

Only the human explicitly requests the skill. These skills are suitable for orchestration commands and intentional workflows.

### Model-invoked

The agent may autonomously choose the skill when the task matches its description.

A user-invoked skill must never be made model-invocable implicitly.

## Skill metadata

The AgentOS internal manifest should support:

```text
name
version
description
invocation mode
requires
optional_recommends
inputs
outputs
tools
permissions
references
evaluation_cases
```

The portable `SKILL.md` frontmatter should remain compatible with supported agents.

## Dependencies

Represent dependencies explicitly. Detect cycles.

Dependencies must resolve to a deterministic execution order or a deterministic error.

## Router skills

Provide a router concept similar to `ask-matt`: given a user goal, recommend or invoke the most appropriate user-invoked workflow.

## Progressive disclosure

Always keep descriptions concise. Load the full skill body only when the skill is selected. Load reference files only when needed.

# Evaluations

Deterministic evaluation cases, one folder per area (see `docs/spec/EVALUATION.md`):

```text
evals/
├── knowledge/  ddd/  context/  skills/  workflow/  feedback/
├── architecture/  memory/  adapters/  end-to-end/
└── baselines/      # measured baselines; thresholds are derived from these, never invented
```

## Conventions

- One case per file, named `<topic>_<NNN>.json` (e.g. `context/payment_webhook_007.json`).
- Every case names the `fixture` it runs against and the deterministic oracle used.
- Every bug found becomes a permanent regression case in the relevant area.
- No LLM or network calls. Same input must produce the same result.
- `evals/thresholds.json` is introduced only once baselines exist (Phase 4 onward).

## Running

```bash
agentos evaluate skills      # exit 0 if every case passes, 3 if any fails
agentos evaluate knowledge
agentos evaluate ddd
agentos evaluate context
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
```

The harness lives in `crates/agentos-evaluation`; `cargo test --workspace` also runs the committed
suite. A case file with an unknown field, an `id` that differs from its file name, or an empty
`oracle` is rejected rather than silently skipped.

## `skills/` (Phase 1)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | one skill directory loads (or fails) with exactly the expected diagnostic codes |
| `discovery` | winning level per skill, overrides, exact diagnostic code set |
| `resolve` | exact dependency order, or the expected error code and cycle path |
| `route` | expected top skill (or `null` for none), `must_not_rank`, or a routing error |
| `permission` | `check(skill, capability)` verdict |
| `validate` | full validation outcome, diagnostic codes and (optionally) the exact skill list |
| `skill_eval` | every skill's own `eval_cases` hold (one result per eval case) |

`fixture` is a directory under `fixtures/` (with optional `project/`, `user/`, `builtin/`
subdirectories, or a bare directory of skills), or `builtin:skills` for the shipped skills.

## `knowledge/` (Phase 2 and 2b)

Phase 2: four profile cases and the `python-fastapi` graph. Phase 2b adds graph cases
`node-express`, `typescript-react`, `go`, `java`, and `ruby-rails`. A case `id` is the file stem.

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `profile` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/profile.json` (classification, maturity, confidence, every signal) |
| `graph` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/graph.json` (node id, type, provenance kind; edge endpoints, relation, provenance kind) |

A graph case passes only when both sets match (recall and precision are `n/n`), every node and edge
has complete provenance, a second scan writes zero rows, and deleting `agentos.db` then scanning
reproduces the same node fingerprints. The case copies the fixture before scanning it.

## `ddd/` (Phase 3)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `domain` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain.json` (node id, type, lifecycle, provenance; edge endpoints, relation, provenance; finding id and kind) |
| `markdown` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain-markdown/*.md` after `domain scan`, `domain propose`, and `domain confirm` of the case's `confirm` id |

A domain case passes only when all three sets match. The detail line reports node, edge, and finding
precision and recall, plus confirmed and canonical counts (both zero on these cases) and whether
provenance is complete. A markdown case passes when the five generated files match the golden bytes.
No timestamp is part of either oracle.

## `context/` (Phase 4)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `context` | `must_include`, `must_exclude`, `required_fragments` on a Context Pack built from `fixtures/<fixture>` after scan and domain scan |

`relevant_files` is the manual file list for `agentos benchmark baseline`. The context engine does
not read it. `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are the measured pack size and irrelevant-token
ratio. A bounded-context id in `must_exclude` also rejects every selected node in that package.
Recall of `must_include` and `required_fragments` must be complete. The detail line reports recall,
precision, tokens, irrelevant tokens, latency, and reproducibility.

## `feedback/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `detect` | sorted provider ids, or an error substring for an invalid override |
| `command` | exact argv |
| `parse` | outcome and, for a failure, file and line from a recorded output file |
| `permission` | outcome `refused` and the marker file is not created |
| `regression` | re-parse of the recorded stdout/stderr still matches `expected_outcome` and diagnostics |

Detection is not a successful validation run. Timeout and crash are runner flags. A recorded text
file cannot express them. Those two cases set the flag on the captured output and expect
`timed_out` or `crashed`.

## `architecture/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `architecture` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/architecture.json` |

A finding matches an expected item when the detector is the same and `paths` contains the expected
path. The case passes only when false positives and false negatives are both zero and a second
analysis returns the same findings. An empty oracle and an empty report is agreement
(`precision 0/0`, `recall 0/0`). No percentage threshold is applied.

## `workflow/` (Phase 6)

| `kind` | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `graph` | ready frontier, join, and bounded concurrency waves |
| `error` | task-graph cycle, missing skill, and zero concurrency |
| `skill_cycle` | skill dependency cycle through the Phase 1 resolver |
| `permission` | a denied capability blocks the step and does not call the runner |
| `resume` | completed steps are not executed again |
| `abort` | abort is persisted, and a second abort is rejected |
| `context` | one Context Pack per step, declared dependency outputs, unrelated fragments excluded |
| `fix` | a bounded fix loop that passes, and one that exhausts the cap |
| `weaken` | deleting a test, removing a test, or dropping an assertion fails the run |
| `transition` | the legal run and step tables, including every illegal edge |
| `workflow` | feature, bugfix, and refactor definitions, including skip reasons |
| `deterministic` | the same task yields the same plan; `--workflow` wins and the task text stays unchanged |

Cases are synthetic. They do not spawn a validation tool or call a model.

# Fixtures

Small, realistic repositories with known ground truth, used by tests and evaluations.

## Convention

```text
fixtures/<name>/
├── README.md        # what the fixture represents and what it is used for
├── ...              # the repository content itself
└── expected/        # ground truth consumed by tests/evaluations (never read by AgentOS itself)
```

- Fixtures are read-only inputs. Tests that need to modify a fixture copy it first with
  `agentos_testkit::copy_fixture("<name>")`.
- Ground truth is reviewed against the extraction rules before it is committed. `expected/` is listed
  in each fixture's `.agentosignore`, so a scan of the fixture does not index the oracle.

## Fixtures

| Name | Phase | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `placeholder` | 0 | Exercises the fixture loader only. No ground truth beyond its own identity. |
| `skills/` | 1 | Small skill trees for manifest parsing, discovery priority, duplicates, broken overrides, dependency cycles, missing dependencies, version constraints, implicit model invocation and broken built-ins. Ground truth lives in `evals/skills/*.json`; see `skills/README.md`. |

| `hybrid-project` | 2 | Source and a specification. Expected: `HYBRID` / `ESTABLISHED`. |
| `python-fastapi` | 2, 3 | Payments, users, notifications, tests, ADR, API, database, CI, container. Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. Domain ground truth in `expected/domain.json` (Payment, Money, PaymentAggregate, `amount > 0`). |
| `node-express` | 2b | Same payments shape in JavaScript (ESM, JSDoc, `extends`). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `typescript-react` | 2b | Same payments shape in TypeScript, plus a React card (`implements`, JSX). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `go` | 2b | Same payments shape in Go (struct embedding, interface, composite literals). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |

# AgentOS

AgentOS is a local-first, agent-agnostic engineering intelligence layer. It gives coding agents
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any other) the right knowledge, skills, workflow, feedback and
guardrails for a task — without replacing the agent.

> Status: **early development**. The CLI can initialise a project, manage portable skills, build a
> derived knowledge graph, assemble a budgeted Context Pack, and run validation providers. Workflow
> and the other engines are not implemented yet.

## Build

Requirements: Rust (stable, edition 2024) and Git. SQLite is bundled; no system install needed.

```bash
cargo build --release
./target/release/agentos --version
```

## Usage

```bash
agentos init              # create .agentos/ (config, profile, derived SQLite index); safe to re-run
agentos doctor            # check root, git, .agentos, config, database, writability
agentos doctor --json     # same, machine-readable
agentos config            # effective configuration and the source of every value

agentos project profile          # classification, maturity, signals (written by init and scan)
agentos scan                     # index the repository; a second run reports 0 changed
agentos knowledge stats          # node, edge and provenance counts
agentos knowledge nodes          # logical ids
agentos knowledge edges
agentos knowledge inspect <id>
agentos knowledge rebuild        # delete the derived graph and scan again

agentos skills list               # skills that won discovery, with level and invocation
agentos skills inspect tdd        # metadata, resolved dependencies, permissions, body
agentos skills inspect tdd --brief  # metadata only; the body is not read
agentos skills validate           # everything, including bodies; exit 3 on errors
agentos skills install ./my-skill # copy a local skill into .agents/skills/ (git URLs: not yet)
agentos skills graph [--format dot]
agentos domain scan               # infer domain nodes; never confirms them
agentos domain contexts
agentos domain terminology
agentos domain map
agentos domain propose            # one lifecycle step toward Proposed
agentos domain confirm <id>       # Proposed → Confirmed, or Confirmed → Canonical
agentos domain reject <id>
agentos domain validate           # exit 3 when canonical evidence has drifted
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
                              # naive file-token baseline; writes evals/baselines/context-baseline.json
agentos context explain "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos context build "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --format json
agentos context stats "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos evaluate skills           # run evals/skills; exit 3 if a case fails
agentos evaluate knowledge        # project profiles and language graph fixtures
agentos evaluate ddd              # domain lifecycle fixtures
agentos evaluate context          # context packs against evals/context
agentos validate detect           # providers selected for this project
agentos validate --kind unit_test --json
agentos validate last             # most recently stored result
agentos validate record-regression <id>
                              # write evals/feedback/<id>.json from a failed result
agentos architecture analyze     # detectors over the knowledge graph; exit 3 if any finding
agentos evaluate feedback         # detection, parsing, permission, regressions
agentos evaluate architecture     # bad and good architecture fixtures
agentos plan "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --workflow feature
agentos run <plan-id> --runner mock
agentos run status <run-id>
agentos run resume <run-id>
agentos run abort <run-id>
agentos evaluate workflow         # plans, scheduler, resume, fix loop
```

Global flags: `--root <PATH>`, `--json`, `-v` / `-vv`, `--log-level <FILTER>`.

### Skills

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md`: YAML front-matter (schema:
[`schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json`](schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json)) plus a markdown body.
Discovery locations, highest priority first:

1. `<root>/.agents/skills/`
2. `<root>/.agentos/skills/`
3. user-level: `--user-skills-dir`, else `AGENTOS_USER_SKILLS_DIR`, else `$HOME/.agentos/skills`
4. built-in skills compiled into `agentos` (from `skills/`; replace with `--builtin-skills-dir` /
   `AGENTOS_BUILTIN_SKILLS_DIR`)

A higher level overrides a lower one. Two skills with the same name at the same level are an error,
and a broken skill hides lower-level copies of the same name instead of silently falling back.

Invocation: `user_invocable` (default `true`) and `model_invocable` (default `false`) are separate.
A model-invocable skill may not require, or route to, a skill that is only user-invocable.
Permissions (`fs.read`, `fs.write`, `shell`, `network`, `browser`) are default-deny.

### Project root

`--root` if given, otherwise the Git top-level of the current directory, otherwise the current
directory.

### Configuration

Resolved per key, later layers winning:

1. built-in defaults
2. `.agentos/config.toml`
3. environment: `AGENTOS_LOG` (`log.level`), `AGENTOS_OUTPUT` (`output.format`)
4. CLI flags: `--log-level` / `-v` / `-vv`, `--json`

| Key | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | `warn` | a level (`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`) or tracing directives such as `agentos_core=debug,warn` |
| `output.format` | `text` | `text`, `json` |

Logs are written to stderr; command results to stdout.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | runtime error |
| 2 | usage error |
| 3 | a check failed: `doctor` critical failure, `skills validate` errors, `evaluate` case failures, a workflow run that is `failed` or `blocked` |

### Project state

```text
.agentos/
├── config.toml          # project configuration (yours to edit; never overwritten)
├── .gitignore           # keeps derived state out of Git
├── project-profile.json # derived classification and signals; rewritten by init and scan
├── agentos.db           # SQLite knowledge index: derived state, safe to delete and rebuild
├── context-cache/       # derived Context Pack cache
├── feedback/            # derived validation results
└── runs/                # derived plans and resumable runs
```

## Development

```bash
scripts/check.sh   # cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

# Architecture

The locked V1 architecture is specified in [spec/ARCHITECTURE.md](spec/ARCHITECTURE.md), with
product principles in [spec/VISION.md](spec/VISION.md) and per-subsystem contracts in `spec/`.

## What exists after Phase 6

Phase 6 adds `agentos-workflow`. It plans a task graph, expands skill dependencies through the
Phase 1 resolver, builds one Phase 4 Context Pack per step, and consumes Phase 5
`ValidationResult` values. Runs are files under `.agentos/runs/`. `MockRunner` is the test
executor. `ManualRunner` prints the step and records a supplied result. There is no model call
and no agent adapter.

## What exists after Phase 5

Phase 5 adds `agentos-feedback` and `agentos-tools`. Validation providers construct commands and
parse output. Every process is started by `agentos-tools` after a shell permission check, with a
timeout and a byte cap on stdout and stderr. Architecture analysis reads the existing knowledge
graph. It does not create another one. Stored results live under `.agentos/feedback/` and are
derived state.

## What exists after Phase 4

Phase 4 adds `agentos-context`. It reads the Phase 2 and Phase 3 graph and returns a Context Pack.
It does not write a second graph. `agentos benchmark baseline` measures naive file tokens before
any pack is built. `agentos context build` projects logical ids, provenance, and lifecycle status
into a pack with a retrieval trace. A cache under `.agentos/context-cache/` is derived state.

## What exists after Phase 3

Phase 3 adds a domain module in `agentos-knowledge`. It writes bounded contexts, tactical concepts,
findings, and lifecycle transitions into the same SQLite index (`domain_nodes`, `domain_edges`,
`domain_transitions`, `domain_findings`). Software nodes stay in the Phase 2 tables. `agentos domain`
confirms or rejects them. Generated markdown is under `.agentos/knowledge/domain/`.

## Crate layout

```text
agentos-cli ─┬─► agentos-config ───► agentos-core
             ├─► agentos-knowledge ─► agentos-core
             ├─► agentos-context ──► agentos-knowledge
             ├─► agentos-skills ─┬─► agentos-core
             │                   └─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-feedback ─┬─► agentos-knowledge
             │                     ├─► agentos-permissions
             │                     └─► agentos-tools ─► agentos-permissions
             ├─► agentos-workflow ─┬─► agentos-skills
             │                     ├─► agentos-context
             │                     ├─► agentos-feedback
             │                     ├─► agentos-permissions
             │                     └─► agentos-tools
             └─► agentos-evaluation ─┬─► agentos-core
                                     ├─► agentos-knowledge
                                     ├─► agentos-context
                                     ├─► agentos-skills
                                     ├─► agentos-permissions
                                     ├─► agentos-feedback
                                     ├─► agentos-tools
                                     └─► agentos-workflow
```

| Crate | Contents |
|---|---|
| `agentos-core` | `fs` (`FileSystem` incl. sorted `read_dir` and streaming `open_read`, `RealFs`, `MemFs`), `git` (`Git`, `GitCli`, `FakeGit`), `root` (project-root detection), `state` (`.agentos/` layout, idempotent `ensure`), `db` (SQLite open, migration runner, read-only `inspect`) |
| `agentos-config` | Layered config resolution (defaults → file → env → CLI) with per-key sources |
| `agentos-permissions` | `Capability`, `PermissionSet`, `PermissionSubject`, `check(subject, capability) -> Decision` (default-deny, with reason) |
| `agentos-skills` | `SKILL.md` front-matter parsing (schema `schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json` + semantic checks), `SkillLoader` (prioritized discovery, front-matter only), `SkillRegistry` (lazy body/reference loading), dependency resolver (topological order, cycle path, semver), rule-based `SkillRouter`, full `validate`, `SkillGraph` (text/DOT), local `install`, built-in skills embedded from `skills/` |
| `agentos-knowledge` | Automatic project profile, ignore-aware scanner, `LanguageExtractor` (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, Ruby), knowledge graph in SQLite (nodes, edges, fragments, FTS5), provenance, domain tables |
| `agentos-context` | Context Pack assembly over that graph: intent, routing, lexical/graph retrieval, budget, trace, cache. `NullSemantic` is the semantic seam |
| `agentos-evaluation` | Deterministic case runner; areas `skills`, `knowledge`, `ddd`, `context`, `feedback`, `architecture`, and `workflow` |
| `agentos-feedback` | `ValidationProvider`, language providers, stored results, architecture detectors over the existing graph |
| `agentos-tools` | Process runner: shell permission, timeout, capped stdout and stderr |
| `agentos-workflow` | Task graph, Phase 1 skill expansion, deterministic scheduler, resumable runs, MockRunner and ManualRunner |
| `agentos-cli` | The `agentos` binary: `init`, `doctor`, `config`, `project profile`, `scan`, `knowledge`, `domain`, `benchmark baseline`, `context`, `skills`, `validate`, `architecture analyze`, `plan`, `run`, `evaluate {skills, knowledge, ddd, context, feedback, architecture, workflow}` |
| `agentos-testkit` | Dev-only: `TempProject`, `CliRunner`, fixture loader |
| all other crates | Compiling stubs, implemented by later phases |

### Skill system data flow

```text
SkillLocation × 4 ─► SkillLoader::discover ─► Discovery { registry, diagnostics }
  (front-matter only)                              │
```

## Project understanding

Project understanding runs before or alongside knowledge extraction and is automatic; the user does not choose “greenfield” vs “existing” as a setup step. It produces a deterministic, evidence-backed project profile that downstream phases consume.

The profile has two dimensions:

- `classification`: `GREENFIELD`, `EXISTING`, or `HYBRID`
- `maturity`: `EMPTY`, `SPECIFIED`, `SKELETON`, `DEVELOPING`, `ESTABLISHED`, or `MATURE`

The detector records the signals used (Git history, source files, build/package manifests, tests, docs/specs, schema/API definitions, CI/container config) plus confidence. Classification is descriptive; the maturity/profile must never invent business facts. Ambiguous cases remain explicitly uncertain rather than forcing a false classification.

Greenfield, existing, and hybrid projects converge into the same Knowledge Model: existing projects are primarily reverse-engineered from evidence, while greenfield projects can contribute declared/proposed knowledge from requirements and design artifacts.

# AgentOS Context Engine

## Goal

Return the smallest context set that preserves the information required to perform the task safely and correctly.
## Never use repository-wide dumping as the default retrieval strategy.

## Retrieval pipeline

```text
User request
  -> intent extraction
  -> domain routing
  -> graph candidate retrieval
  -> structural expansion
  -> semantic/lexical retrieval
  -> relevance ranking
  -> dependency / constraint enrichment
  -> token budgeting
  -> Context Pack
```

## Context Pack

A Context Pack contains:

```text
task
intent
budget
selected_nodes
selected_fragments
terminology
architecture
constraints
invariants
decisions
tests
exclusions
retrieval_trace
```

## Selection principles

Priority order:

1. mandatory task constraints
2. directly relevant domain concepts
3. directly relevant architecture
4. explicit decisions/ADRs
5. relevant invariants and tests
6. directly relevant code fragments
7. supporting context
8. historical/background information

Remove low-priority context first when over budget.

## Retrieval methods

Use multiple complementary methods:

- exact/lexical search
- structural graph traversal
- symbol dependency expansion
- semantic retrieval when enabled

Vector similarity is a retrieval aid, not the system's source of truth.

## Explainability

Every Context Pack should include a retrieval trace sufficient to answer:
- why was this item selected?
- why was this item excluded?
- what relationship caused expansion?
- what source supports the assertion?
- what was the token estimate?

## Context caching

Persist successful task-to-context patterns. Reuse them only when the underlying knowledge fingerprints have not changed.

## Evaluation metrics

At minimum:

- required-context recall
- irrelevant-context rate
- token count
- token reduction versus baseline
- retrieval latency
- reproducibility

Do not optimize token count at the expense of required knowledge recall.

# Domain-Driven Design Contract

AgentOS treats DDD knowledge as explicit project knowledge, not unquestioned LLM output.

## Strategic design

Represent:
- bounded contexts
- ubiquitous language
- context map
- anti-corruption layers
- upstream/downstream relationships
- integration direction

## Tactical design

Represent:
- entities
- value objects
- aggregates and aggregate roots
- invariants
- domain services
- repositories
- policies
- domain events

## Truth lifecycle

Domain assertions use:

`Observed -> Inferred -> Proposed -> Confirmed -> Canonical`

Inference may create `Inferred` or `Proposed` knowledge only. It can never silently create `Confirmed` or `Canonical` knowledge.

## Ubiquitous language

`.agentos/knowledge/domain/ubiquitous-language.md` is the human-readable canonical terminology artifact. Conflicts and synonyms are findings, not automatic merges.

## Aggregate discipline

Aggregates define transactional boundaries and protect business invariants. AgentOS should flag direct mutation or cross-aggregate logic when evidence shows the existing architecture enforces aggregate boundaries.

## Hexagonal architecture

When applicable, AgentOS models the domain core separately from ports and adapters:

`Domain -> Ports -> Adapters`

Infrastructure must not leak into the domain without an explicit, evidenced design decision.

## Corrective policies

Where invariants cannot be enforced synchronously, a corrective policy may periodically detect, flag, or repair inconsistent state. Such policies must be explicit project knowledge and carry provenance.

The Feedback Engine turns objective engineering signals into structured feedback that can be consumed by workflows and agents.

## Provider model

Providers implement capabilities such as:
- test execution
- static type checking
- linting
- build/compile
- browser validation
- architecture checks

The core asks for capabilities; technology adapters supply the project-specific implementation.

## Feedback result

Every validation result should record:
- provider kind
- target
- command/capability used
- exit status

Deterministic evaluation cases, one folder per area (see `docs/spec/EVALUATION.md`):

```text

├── knowledge/  ddd/  context/  skills/  workflow/  feedback/
├── architecture/  memory/  adapters/  end-to-end/
```

## Conventions

- One case per file, named `<topic>_<NNN>.json` (e.g. `context/payment_webhook_007.json`).
- Every case names the `fixture` it runs against and the deterministic oracle used.
- Every bug found becomes a permanent regression case in the relevant area.
- No LLM or network calls. Same input must produce the same result.
- `evals/thresholds.json` is introduced only once baselines exist (Phase 4 onward).

## Running

```bash
agentos evaluate skills      # exit 0 if every case passes, 3 if any fails
agentos evaluate knowledge
agentos evaluate ddd
agentos evaluate context
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
```

The harness lives in `crates/agentos-evaluation`; `cargo test --workspace` also runs the committed
suite. A case file with an unknown field, an `id` that differs from its file name, or an empty
`oracle` is rejected rather than silently skipped.

## `skills/` (Phase 1)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | one skill directory loads (or fails) with exactly the expected diagnostic codes |
| `discovery` | winning level per skill, overrides, exact diagnostic code set |
| `resolve` | exact dependency order, or the expected error code and cycle path |
| `route` | expected top skill (or `null` for none), `must_not_rank`, or a routing error |
| `permission` | `check(skill, capability)` verdict |
| `validate` | full validation outcome, diagnostic codes and (optionally) the exact skill list |
| `skill_eval` | every skill's own `eval_cases` hold (one result per eval case) |

`fixture` is a directory under `fixtures/` (with optional `project/`, `user/`, `builtin/`
subdirectories, or a bare directory of skills), or `builtin:skills` for the shipped skills.

## `knowledge/` (Phase 2 and 2b)

Phase 2: four profile cases and the `python-fastapi` graph. Phase 2b adds graph cases
`node-express`, `typescript-react`, `go`, `java`, and `ruby-rails`. A case `id` is the file stem.

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `profile` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/profile.json` (classification, maturity, confidence, every signal) |
| `graph` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/graph.json` (node id, type, provenance kind; edge endpoints, relation, provenance kind) |

A graph case passes only when both sets match (recall and precision are `n/n`), every node and edge
has complete provenance, a second scan writes zero rows, and deleting `agentos.db` then scanning
reproduces the same node fingerprints. The case copies the fixture before scanning it.

## `ddd/` (Phase 3)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `domain` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain.json` (node id, type, lifecycle, provenance; edge endpoints, relation, provenance; finding id and kind) |
| `markdown` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain-markdown/*.md` after `domain scan`, `domain propose`, and `domain confirm` of the case's `confirm` id |

A domain case passes only when all three sets match. The detail line reports node, edge, and finding
precision and recall, plus confirmed and canonical counts (both zero on these cases) and whether
provenance is complete. A markdown case passes when the five generated files match the golden bytes.
No timestamp is part of either oracle.

## `context/` (Phase 4)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `context` | `must_include`, `must_exclude`, `required_fragments` on a Context Pack built from `fixtures/<fixture>` after scan and domain scan |

`relevant_files` is the manual file list for `agentos benchmark baseline`. The context engine does
not read it. `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are the measured pack size and irrelevant-token
ratio. A bounded-context id in `must_exclude` also rejects every selected node in that package.
Recall of `must_include` and `required_fragments` must be complete. The detail line reports recall,
precision, tokens, irrelevant tokens, latency, and reproducibility.

## `feedback/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `detect` | sorted provider ids, or an error substring for an invalid override |
| `command` | exact argv |
| `parse` | outcome and, for a failure, file and line from a recorded output file |
| `permission` | outcome `refused` and the marker file is not created |
| `regression` | re-parse of the recorded stdout/stderr still matches `expected_outcome` and diagnostics |

Detection is not a successful validation run. Timeout and crash are runner flags. A recorded text
file cannot express them. Those two cases set the flag on the captured output and expect
`timed_out` or `crashed`.

## `architecture/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `architecture` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/architecture.json` |

A finding matches an expected item when the detector is the same and `paths` contains the expected
path. The case passes only when false positives and false negatives are both zero and a second
analysis returns the same findings. An empty oracle and an empty report is agreement
(`precision 0/0`, `recall 0/0`). No percentage threshold is applied.

## `workflow/` (Phase 6)

| `kind` | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `graph` | ready frontier, join, and bounded concurrency waves |
| `error` | task-graph cycle, missing skill, and zero concurrency |
| `skill_cycle` | skill dependency cycle through the Phase 1 resolver |
| `permission` | a denied capability blocks the step and does not call the runner |
| `resume` | completed steps are not executed again |
| `abort` | abort is persisted, and a second abort is rejected |
| `context` | one Context Pack per step, declared dependency outputs, unrelated fragments excluded |
| `fix` | a bounded fix loop that passes, and one that exhausts the cap |
| `weaken` | deleting a test, removing a test, or dropping an assertion fails the run |
| `transition` | the legal run and step tables, including every illegal edge |
| `workflow` | feature, bugfix, and refactor definitions, including skip reasons |
| `deterministic` | the same task yields the same plan; `--workflow` wins and the task text stays unchanged |

Cases are synthetic. They do not spawn a validation tool or call a model.

# Architecture review

## When to use
You need an evidence-based picture of how the code is structured: before a large change, after
growth, or when boundaries seem to be eroding. This skill only assesses; it does not change code.

## Inputs
- The scope to assess.
- Optional intended rules (layers, allowed dependency directions).

## Procedure
1. Map the modules in scope and the dependencies between them.
2. Compare the dependency directions with the intended rules (or infer and state them).
3. Identify cycles, layering violations, high coupling and shallow modules.
4. For each finding, record concrete evidence (file, import or call site).
5. Rank findings by impact and suggest which to address first.

## Outputs
A report of violations and risks with evidence, ranked by impact.

## Must not
- Modify code; use `improve-codebase-architecture` for changes.
- Report a violation without evidence.
- Assume a framework or language convention without checking the code.

## Validation
Every finding cites evidence a reviewer can open, and the dependency map covers the whole scope.
# Code review

## When to use
A concrete set of changes (diff, branch, pull request) needs feedback before it is merged.

## Inputs
- The changes to review.
- Optional: the project's coding standards and the requirement the change implements.

## Procedure
1. Read the requirement, then the full diff, before commenting.
2. Check correctness: logic errors, edge cases, error handling, concurrency.
3. Check tests: changed behaviour is tested, tests can fail, no test was weakened.
4. Check standards and readability against the project's documented rules.
5. Report findings ordered by severity, each with location and a suggested fix.

## Outputs
A review: findings (blocking, should-fix, nit) with file and line, plus an overall verdict.

## Must not
- Edit the code under review.
- Report style preferences as blocking unless a documented standard requires it.
- Review architecture beyond the diff; recommend `architecture-review` instead.

## Validation
Every finding points to a specific location in the diff and states why it matters.
# Improve codebase architecture

## When to use
The human has decided to restructure code, usually after an `architecture-review` (which runs
first). This skill is user-invoked only because it makes broad changes.

## Inputs
- Findings from `architecture-review`.
- The structural goal.

## Procedure
1. Pick the highest-impact finding and state the target structure for it.
2. Make sure tests cover the behaviour of the code that will move; add tests first if not.
3. Apply one behaviour-preserving refactoring step.
4. Run the full checks; revert the step if anything fails.
5. Repeat until the finding is resolved, then re-run `architecture-review` on the scope.

## Outputs
Small, separately verified refactoring steps and a before/after summary.

## Must not
- Change behaviour while restructuring.
- Combine refactoring with feature work.
- Start without an explicit request from the human.

## Validation
All checks pass after every step, and the follow-up architecture review no longer reports the
addressed finding.

# AgentOS

AgentOS is a local-first, agent-agnostic engineering intelligence layer. It gives coding agents
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any other) the right knowledge, skills, workflow, feedback and
guardrails for a task — without replacing the agent.

> Status: **early development**. The CLI can initialise a project, manage portable skills, build a
> derived knowledge graph, assemble a budgeted Context Pack, and run validation providers. Workflow
> and the other engines are not implemented yet.

## Build

Requirements: Rust (stable, edition 2024) and Git. SQLite is bundled; no system install needed.

```bash
cargo build --release
./target/release/agentos --version
```

## Usage

```bash
agentos init              # create .agentos/ (config, profile, derived SQLite index); safe to re-run
agentos doctor            # check root, git, .agentos, config, database, writability
agentos doctor --json     # same, machine-readable
agentos config            # effective configuration and the source of every value

agentos project profile          # classification, maturity, signals (written by init and scan)
agentos scan                     # index the repository; a second run reports 0 changed
agentos knowledge stats          # node, edge and provenance counts
agentos knowledge nodes          # logical ids
agentos knowledge edges
agentos knowledge inspect <id>
agentos knowledge rebuild        # delete the derived graph and scan again

agentos skills list               # skills that won discovery, with level and invocation
agentos skills inspect tdd        # metadata, resolved dependencies, permissions, body
agentos skills inspect tdd --brief  # metadata only; the body is not read
agentos skills validate           # everything, including bodies; exit 3 on errors
agentos skills install ./my-skill # copy a local skill into .agents/skills/ (git URLs: not yet)
agentos skills graph [--format dot]
agentos domain scan               # infer domain nodes; never confirms them
agentos domain contexts
agentos domain terminology
agentos domain map
agentos domain propose            # one lifecycle step toward Proposed
agentos domain confirm <id>       # Proposed → Confirmed, or Confirmed → Canonical
agentos domain reject <id>
agentos domain validate           # exit 3 when canonical evidence has drifted
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
                              # naive file-token baseline; writes evals/baselines/context-baseline.json
agentos context explain "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos context build "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --format json
agentos context stats "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos evaluate skills           # run evals/skills; exit 3 if a case fails
agentos evaluate knowledge        # project profiles and language graph fixtures
agentos evaluate ddd              # domain lifecycle fixtures
agentos evaluate context          # context packs against evals/context
agentos validate detect           # providers selected for this project
agentos validate --kind unit_test --json
agentos validate last             # most recently stored result
agentos validate record-regression <id>
                              # write evals/feedback/<id>.json from a failed result
agentos architecture analyze     # detectors over the knowledge graph; exit 3 if any finding
agentos evaluate feedback         # detection, parsing, permission, regressions
agentos evaluate architecture     # bad and good architecture fixtures
agentos plan "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --workflow feature
agentos run <plan-id> --runner mock
agentos run status <run-id>
agentos run resume <run-id>
agentos run abort <run-id>
agentos evaluate workflow         # plans, scheduler, resume, fix loop
```

Global flags: `--root <PATH>`, `--json`, `-v` / `-vv`, `--log-level <FILTER>`.

### Skills

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md`: YAML front-matter (schema:
[`schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json`](schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json)) plus a markdown body.
Discovery locations, highest priority first:

1. `<root>/.agents/skills/`
2. `<root>/.agentos/skills/`
3. user-level: `--user-skills-dir`, else `AGENTOS_USER_SKILLS_DIR`, else `$HOME/.agentos/skills`
4. built-in skills compiled into `agentos` (from `skills/`; replace with `--builtin-skills-dir` /
   `AGENTOS_BUILTIN_SKILLS_DIR`)

A higher level overrides a lower one. Two skills with the same name at the same level are an error,
and a broken skill hides lower-level copies of the same name instead of silently falling back.

Invocation: `user_invocable` (default `true`) and `model_invocable` (default `false`) are separate.
A model-invocable skill may not require, or route to, a skill that is only user-invocable.
Permissions (`fs.read`, `fs.write`, `shell`, `network`, `browser`) are default-deny.

### Project root

`--root` if given, otherwise the Git top-level of the current directory, otherwise the current
directory.

### Configuration

Resolved per key, later layers winning:

1. built-in defaults
2. `.agentos/config.toml`
3. environment: `AGENTOS_LOG` (`log.level`), `AGENTOS_OUTPUT` (`output.format`)
4. CLI flags: `--log-level` / `-v` / `-vv`, `--json`

| Key | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | `warn` | a level (`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`) or tracing directives such as `agentos_core=debug,warn` |
| `output.format` | `text` | `text`, `json` |

Logs are written to stderr; command results to stdout.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | runtime error |
| 2 | usage error |
| 3 | a check failed: `doctor` critical failure, `skills validate` errors, `evaluate` case failures, a workflow run that is `failed` or `blocked` |

```text
├── config.toml          # project configuration (yours to edit; never overwritten)
├── .gitignore           # keeps derived state out of Git

├── agentos.db           # SQLite knowledge index: derived state, safe to delete and rebuild
├── context-cache/       # derived Context Pack cache
```

# AgentOS Evaluation System

Evaluation is a first-class subsystem beginning in Phase 0.

## Test layers

1. Unit tests
2. Integration tests
3. Fixture repository tests
4. Golden/retrieval tests
5. End-to-end workflow evaluations
6. Adapter compatibility tests
7. Regression tests for every discovered defect

## Fixture philosophy

Fixtures are small, realistic repositories with known ground truth. Include multiple technology stacks and deliberately bad architectures.

Recommended fixtures:
- `python-fastapi/`
- `node-express/`
- `typescript-react/`
- `go/`
- `java/`
- `ruby-rails/`
- `bad-architecture/`

## Golden case shape

```json
{
  "task": "Add retry support to payment webhook processing",
  "must_include": ["domain.payment.entity.Payment"],
  "must_not_include": ["fleet", "analytics"],
  "required_fragments": ["webhook_handler.py", "test_webhook_idempotency.py"]
}
```

Exact thresholds are derived from measured baselines, never invented.

## Core metrics

Knowledge: node precision/recall, edge precision/recall, provenance coverage.
DDD: context detection, terminology ambiguity, invariant mapping, lifecycle correctness.
Context: required-context recall, irrelevant-context rate, token count, reduction versus baseline, latency, reproducibility.
Skills: discovery, routing, dependency correctness, permission enforcement.
Feedback: validation detection and structured diagnostics.
Architecture: known-violation detection.
Workflow: execution order, ready frontier, resume behavior, bounded repair loops.
Memory: retrieval precision, staleness, forget semantics, secret redaction.
Adapters: install, idempotency, compatibility, uninstall safety.

## Evaluation traceability

Every context and major workflow evaluation should make it possible to answer:
- what inputs were used?
- what knowledge was selected?
- what was excluded and why?
- what tools/permissions were granted?
- what validation evidence was produced?

## Release gate

A release is green only when the relevant automated tests and evaluations pass, regression coverage remains green, and all phase gates are approved.

## Additions

**Golden case optional fields:** `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are `null` until the Phase 4 baseline has been measured; only then are they set. Cases also record `fixture`, the deterministic oracle used, and (for context cases) `required_fragments`.

**Eval folders:** `evals/{knowledge,ddd,context,skills,workflow,feedback,architecture,memory,adapters,end-to-end,baselines}/`.

**Evaluate intermediate artifacts, not only final code:** project profile, knowledge graph, context pack, plan, permissions, feedback, final changes.

**Regression rule:** every bug becomes a permanent case (e.g. `evals/context/payment_webhook_007.json` for "Notifications context retrieved for a Payment task"). `agentos evaluate <area>` must keep it green.

**Dashboard (Phase 10):** `agentos evaluate` prints Knowledge / DDD / Context / Skills / Feedback / Adapters sections and an overall PASS/FAIL using REAL measured values; thresholds come from `evals/thresholds.json`, derived from baselines.

**Known-bad fixture:** `fixtures/bad-architecture/` (circular dependencies, fat controllers, DB calls in domain, duplicate terminology, broken invariants, shallow modules, missing tests) with ground truth.

# Evaluations

Deterministic evaluation cases, one folder per area (see `docs/spec/EVALUATION.md`):

```text
evals/
├── knowledge/  ddd/  context/  skills/  workflow/  feedback/
├── architecture/  memory/  adapters/  end-to-end/
└── baselines/      # measured baselines; thresholds are derived from these, never invented
```

## Conventions

- One case per file, named `<topic>_<NNN>.json` (e.g. `context/payment_webhook_007.json`).
- Every case names the `fixture` it runs against and the deterministic oracle used.
- Every bug found becomes a permanent regression case in the relevant area.
- No LLM or network calls. Same input must produce the same result.
- `evals/thresholds.json` is introduced only once baselines exist (Phase 4 onward).

## Running

```bash
agentos evaluate skills      # exit 0 if every case passes, 3 if any fails
agentos evaluate knowledge
agentos evaluate ddd
agentos evaluate context
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
```

The harness lives in `crates/agentos-evaluation`; `cargo test --workspace` also runs the committed
suite. A case file with an unknown field, an `id` that differs from its file name, or an empty
`oracle` is rejected rather than silently skipped.

## `skills/` (Phase 1)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | one skill directory loads (or fails) with exactly the expected diagnostic codes |
| `discovery` | winning level per skill, overrides, exact diagnostic code set |
| `resolve` | exact dependency order, or the expected error code and cycle path |
| `route` | expected top skill (or `null` for none), `must_not_rank`, or a routing error |
| `permission` | `check(skill, capability)` verdict |
| `validate` | full validation outcome, diagnostic codes and (optionally) the exact skill list |
| `skill_eval` | every skill's own `eval_cases` hold (one result per eval case) |

`fixture` is a directory under `fixtures/` (with optional `project/`, `user/`, `builtin/`
subdirectories, or a bare directory of skills), or `builtin:skills` for the shipped skills.

## `knowledge/` (Phase 2 and 2b)

Phase 2: four profile cases and the `python-fastapi` graph. Phase 2b adds graph cases
`node-express`, `typescript-react`, `go`, `java`, and `ruby-rails`. A case `id` is the file stem.

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `profile` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/profile.json` (classification, maturity, confidence, every signal) |
| `graph` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/graph.json` (node id, type, provenance kind; edge endpoints, relation, provenance kind) |

A graph case passes only when both sets match (recall and precision are `n/n`), every node and edge
has complete provenance, a second scan writes zero rows, and deleting `agentos.db` then scanning
reproduces the same node fingerprints. The case copies the fixture before scanning it.

## `ddd/` (Phase 3)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `domain` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain.json` (node id, type, lifecycle, provenance; edge endpoints, relation, provenance; finding id and kind) |
| `markdown` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain-markdown/*.md` after `domain scan`, `domain propose`, and `domain confirm` of the case's `confirm` id |

A domain case passes only when all three sets match. The detail line reports node, edge, and finding
precision and recall, plus confirmed and canonical counts (both zero on these cases) and whether
provenance is complete. A markdown case passes when the five generated files match the golden bytes.
No timestamp is part of either oracle.

## `context/` (Phase 4)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `context` | `must_include`, `must_exclude`, `required_fragments` on a Context Pack built from `fixtures/<fixture>` after scan and domain scan |

`relevant_files` is the manual file list for `agentos benchmark baseline`. The context engine does
not read it. `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are the measured pack size and irrelevant-token
ratio. A bounded-context id in `must_exclude` also rejects every selected node in that package.
Recall of `must_include` and `required_fragments` must be complete. The detail line reports recall,
precision, tokens, irrelevant tokens, latency, and reproducibility.

## `feedback/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `detect` | sorted provider ids, or an error substring for an invalid override |
| `command` | exact argv |
| `parse` | outcome and, for a failure, file and line from a recorded output file |
| `permission` | outcome `refused` and the marker file is not created |
| `regression` | re-parse of the recorded stdout/stderr still matches `expected_outcome` and diagnostics |

Detection is not a successful validation run. Timeout and crash are runner flags. A recorded text
file cannot express them. Those two cases set the flag on the captured output and expect
`timed_out` or `crashed`.

## `architecture/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `architecture` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/architecture.json` |

A finding matches an expected item when the detector is the same and `paths` contains the expected
path. The case passes only when false positives and false negatives are both zero and a second
analysis returns the same findings. An empty oracle and an empty report is agreement
(`precision 0/0`, `recall 0/0`). No percentage threshold is applied.

## `workflow/` (Phase 6)

| `kind` | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `graph` | ready frontier, join, and bounded concurrency waves |
| `error` | task-graph cycle, missing skill, and zero concurrency |
| `skill_cycle` | skill dependency cycle through the Phase 1 resolver |
| `permission` | a denied capability blocks the step and does not call the runner |
| `resume` | completed steps are not executed again |
| `abort` | abort is persisted, and a second abort is rejected |
| `context` | one Context Pack per step, declared dependency outputs, unrelated fragments excluded |
| `fix` | a bounded fix loop that passes, and one that exhausts the cap |
| `weaken` | deleting a test, removing a test, or dropping an assertion fails the run |
| `transition` | the legal run and step tables, including every illegal edge |
| `workflow` | feature, bugfix, and refactor definitions, including skip reasons |
| `deterministic` | the same task yields the same plan; `--workflow` wins and the task text stays unchanged |

Cases are synthetic. They do not spawn a validation tool or call a model.
